saints.name: Saint Makarios of Corinth
saints.region: Corinth; Mount Athos; Patmos; Chios, Greece

summary.text: Saint Makarios was Archbishop of Corinth and a monastic teacher associated with Saint Nikodemos the Hagiorite and the publication of the Philokalia.

blocks.text: Born at Trikala in Corinth in 1731, he belonged to the Notaras family and was baptized Michael. He taught young people in Corinth without payment before becoming its archbishop in 1764.

blocks.text: War forced him away from Corinth, and another archbishop was appointed. He later visited Mount Athos, where disputes over memorial services affected monastic life. He founded a settlement on Patmos and eventually lived on Chios, teaching, hearing confessions, and assisting people in need.

blocks.text: Saint Makarios died on April 17, 1805. He was buried beside the church of the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul on Chios. His relics were recovered in 1808. This account does not describe martyrdom.

blocks.text: He helped secure support for publishing the Philokalia and the catechism of Metropolitan Platon of Moscow. His collaboration with Saint Nikodemos links his episcopal ministry with the transmission of older Orthodox spiritual writings.
